Information cutoff: 2026-03-31T16:00:00-04:00. Use only information publicly available at or before this timestamp.
This is the information boundary; reporting periods, valuation dates, and forecast targets are specified below.
Working time limit: 7200 seconds.

Company: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN)
Target period: 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30.

Strict information cutoff: 2026-03-31T16:00:00-04:00. Use only information publicly available on or before this timestamp.

Amazon.com will report results for the quarter ending June 30, 2026. Using only information available up to March 31, 2026, forecast what the company will report for that quarter.

Give point estimates in USD billions for consolidated net sales, consolidated operating income, AWS segment net sales and AWS segment operating income, along with the implied year-over-year growth rates and operating margins for the quarter.

Show the bridge from Amazon's reported results and management guidance to your estimates, including the growth and margin assumptions and the cost and mix factors behind them. Set out the key uncertainties and sensitivities: what could move the numbers materially, and in which direction.

Make each assumption explicit and show enough of the arithmetic that a reader can follow how the four estimates are built up.

Submission method (required):
Call `submit_answer` as the final response. In `structured_output`, submit:
- $.net_sales_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 consolidated net sales in USD billions.
- $.operating_income_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 consolidated operating income in USD billions.
- $.aws_net_sales_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 AWS segment net sales in USD billions.
- $.aws_operating_income_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 AWS segment operating income in USD billions.
Cite at least 2 distinct cutoff-database documents. Include material calculations and any file explicitly required by the question.

rubrics.criterion: The implied year-over-year growth rates in Amazon.com's Q2 2026 forecast are derived from the four submitted point estimates and the Q2 2025 comparatives reported by the company for the quarter ended June 30, 2025.
rubrics.pass_condition: Each of the four stated growth rates matches the percentage change from the corresponding Q2 2025 comparative to the submitted estimate, within one percentage point.

Strict information cutoff: 2026-03-31T16:00:00-04:00. Use only information publicly available on or before this timestamp.

Amazon.com will report results for the quarter ending June 30, 2026. Using only information available up to March 31, 2026, forecast what the company will report for that quarter.

Give point estimates in USD billions for consolidated net sales, consolidated operating income, AWS segment net sales and AWS segment operating income, along with the implied year-over-year growth rates and operating margins for the quarter.

Show the bridge from Amazon's reported results and management guidance to your estimates, including the growth and margin assumptions and the cost and mix factors behind them. Set out the key uncertainties and sensitivities: what could move the numbers materially, and in which direction.

Make each assumption explicit and show enough of the arithmetic that a reader can follow how the four estimates are built up.

Submission method (required):
Call `submit_answer` as the final response. In `structured_output`, submit:
- $.net_sales_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 consolidated net sales in USD billions.
- $.operating_income_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 consolidated operating income in USD billions.
- $.aws_net_sales_usd_bn: Point forecast of Q2 2026 AWS segment net sales in USD billions.

judge_rubrics.title: Depreciation ramp evidence
judge_rubrics.criterion: Amazon's Q2 2026 cost assumptions reflect the investment and depreciation ramp, supported by at least one disclosed figure on capital spending or depreciation such as the approximately USD 200 billion 2026 capital plan or fiscal 2025 property depreciation of about USD 41.9 billion.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: At least one disclosed capital expenditure or depreciation figure is cited, and the stated margin or cost assumptions account for its directional effect on Q2 2026 costs.
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Check that at least one disclosed capex or depreciation figure informs the cost assumptions, for example the approximately 200 billion 2026 capital plan, the rise in property and equipment depreciation from 32.1 billion in 2024 to 41.9 billion in 2025, the increase in net additions to property and equipment from 85.8 billion to 142.4 billion, or the roughly 125 billion 2025 cash capex baseline. The stated direction should reflect rising depreciation pressure as capacity comes online. Accept equivalent disclosures; fail if no such figure appears or its directional effect is ignored.

direct_evidence_materials.supported_claim: Accelerating depreciation and investment trend that pressures 2026 margins.

judge_rubrics.financial_concept: Amazon Q2 2026 AWS segment net sales
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Check that the AWS revenue growth assumption is tied to at least one cutoff-valid datapoint with magnitude, for example AWS net sales up 24 percent year over year in Q4 2025, up 20.2 percent in Q3 2025, about 3.9GW of power added over twelve months, the 200 billion backlog, or the expanded OpenAI commitment of approximately 2GW and 100 billion over eight years. Accept equivalent demand, capacity, or backlog evidence. Fail when no quantified AWS demand or capacity datapoint supports the growth assumption.

judge_rubrics.title: Revenue-side sensitivities
judge_rubrics.criterion: The outlook sets out the revenue-side sensitivities of Amazon's Q2 2026 forecast, covering the factors that could move the net sales estimates materially and the direction of each effect.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: At least one specific factor is named with the direction in which it would move Q2 2026 revenue and a rough magnitude, such as a percentage-point or currency range.
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Judge whether the answer states revenue-side sensitivities with direction and rough magnitude. Plausible factors include the favorable FX effect of roughly 150 to 180 basis points disclosed in late 2025 and early 2026, AWS capacity timing and demand commitments, consumer demand and pricing, and the 2026 physical-store closures. Accept equivalent factor sets. Fail when no revenue factor is given with direction and rough size, or when a stated direction contradicts the cited evidence.

judge_rubrics.title: Profit-side sensitivities
judge_rubrics.criterion: The profit-side sensitivities of Amazon's Q2 2026 forecast are identified, covering the factors that could move the operating income estimates materially and the direction of each effect.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: At least one specific factor is named with the direction in which it would move Q2 2026 operating income and a rough magnitude or range.
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Judge whether the answer states profit-side sensitivities with direction and rough magnitude. Plausible factors include depreciation growth from the approximately 200 billion 2026 capital plan, normalization of 2025 charges, Amazon Leo costs of about 1 billion year over year, International investment and pricing, AWS margin mix including seasonal stock-based compensation, and retail cost efficiency. Accept any equivalent factor set. Fail when no profit factor is given with direction and rough size.

judge_rubrics.title: Quantified uncertainty range
judge_rubrics.criterion: The uncertainty around Amazon's Q2 2026 estimates is conveyed with magnitude, not only direction, through a stated range or bounded scenario for at least one of the four forecast metrics.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: A numeric range or band, such as a stated percentage spread or a low-to-high interval, accompanies at least one of the four Q2 2026 point estimates.
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Check whether at least one of the four Q2 2026 estimates carries an explicit numeric range, band, or bounded scenario. The width is not prescribed; a clearly bounded range linked to the stated sensitivities passes, as does a per-metric sensitivity stated as plus or minus a percentage. Fail when uncertainty is expressed only qualitatively with no numeric bound on any of the four metrics.

judge_rubrics.title: Unguided quarter limitation
judge_rubrics.criterion: The answer acknowledges a central limitation of the forecast: Amazon's results for the quarter ending June 30, 2026 were not yet guided at the cutoff, so the quarter must be extrapolated from guided and reported data.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: The answer notes that no Q2 2026 management guidance was available at the cutoff and identifies its reliance on extrapolation from earlier guidance or reported results, or states an equivalent limitation.
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Check whether the answer flags that the June 2026 quarter was unguided at the cutoff, for example by noting that the latest guidance covers only Q1 2026 and that the Q2 view extends the trajectory from guided and reported data, or an equivalent statement of extrapolation reliance. Fail when the estimates are presented without acknowledging that they extend beyond the guidance horizon.

judge_rubrics.title: Growth versus margin net read
judge_rubrics.criterion: The analysis resolves whether Amazon's Q2 2026 profitability is led by revenue growth and mix or held back by margin pressure, and that net read is consistent with the submitted estimate against the prior-year quarter.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: A net characterization of the quarter is present, and its direction agrees with the change implied by the submitted consolidated operating income estimate relative to about USD 19.2 billion in the June 2025 quarter.
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Check whether the answer offers a net read on whether growth and mix support Q2 2026 profitability or margin pressure dominates, and whether that read matches the direction of the submitted consolidated operating income estimate versus the reported 19,171 million for the June 2025 quarter. Either verdict passes if internally consistent, including a roughly flat read where the estimate sits near the prior-year level. Fail if no net read is stated or if the stated direction contradicts the estimate.

judge_rubrics.criterion: Amazon's net read on Q2 2026 profitability rests on drivers that the analysis also quantifies in its bridge to the four estimates.

Fail when the net read rests on a driver the bridge does not quantify or contradicts the bridge's own numbers.

judge_rubrics.title: AWS segment nesting
judge_rubrics.criterion: Amazon reports AWS as one segment within consolidated results, so the forecasted AWS net sales and AWS operating income are each smaller than the corresponding consolidated Q2 2026 estimates.
judge_rubrics.pass_condition: The submitted AWS net sales and AWS operating income are both below the submitted consolidated net sales and consolidated operating income, leaving a positive non-AWS operating contribution.
judge_rubrics.financial_concept: Amazon Q2 2026 AWS segment net sales
judge_rubrics.expected_reasoning: Check the internal structure of the four estimates: AWS is a reportable segment inside consolidated results, so AWS net sales and AWS operating income must each sit below the consolidated figures and the implied non-AWS operating contribution (historically North America plus International) must be positive. Fail if AWS amounts exceed or equal their consolidated counterparts, or if the implied non-AWS operating result is negative.
